title: George Mitchell and Jelly Roll Morton's Red Hot Peppers
summary: He likes cornetist George Mitchell on Red Hot Peppers records; Crawford notes a growl on a tune sounds like Paul Mares.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: We were talking about Jolly Roll too. You listening to a lot of Jolly Roll?

Uh... Well, uh, I had one or two records with the, uh, the Hot Peppers, Red Hot Peppers. And, uh, this fellow that plays Cornet in their group, uh, a guy by the name of George Mitchell. He was, uh, he was a good Cornetist. I liked his style. And, uh, I'll say once before, he appears to be a musician that might have come from one of these orchestra pits. He plays that type of stuff, you know. He's good. He's really good.
I heard you play something one time on Lillingberg. It sounded like Paul Morell, but you said you never heard any of Paul Morell's stuff, huh?
No, no, no. That's, uh, oh, you're talking about that first note on Lillingberg, that growl, huh?
I don't know. I thought it might have sound good then, so I just used it, see? See, I have to invent my stuff as I go along, so yeah.
